question.worked_solution:
The area bounded by a polar curve is given by

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}(\theta )\text{d}\theta \,.
$$

When $r(\theta )=2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $, ${\theta }_{1}=-\frac{\pi }{2}$ and ${\theta }_{2}=\frac{\pi }{2}$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ))\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\theta \,{|}_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )\,{|}_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2} \\  & =(\frac{\pi }{2}-(-\frac{\pi }{2}))+\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\pi )) \\  & =\pi +0 \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
